dexametha-sone, cortisol, aldosterone, and progesterone induce growth inhibition, cell spread, focal adhesions, and p21(CIP/WAF1) in PR-transfected breast cancer cells, whereas they have little or no effects on vector-transfected breast cells.
glucocorticoids and aldosterone mimic progesterone by cross-talk with progsterone receptor to induce significant cell growth inhibition and cell spreading in breast cancer cells.
glucocorticoids and progesterone share overlapping activities in regulating focal adhesion and cell proliferation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the cross-talk of PR with other steroid receptors in regulating cell growth.
cross-talk between cortisoids and PR, which may have important implications in the pathophysiology of breast cancer.
the mechanism of progesterone-like action of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids in breast cancer cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
PR is a key mediator in the regulation of progesterone-like growth inhibition and focal adhesion.
corticosteroids mimic the effects of PR in inducing focal adhesion but have no effect on cell proliferation.
PR is a steroid hormone receptor that is capable of mediating the effects of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids in breast cancer cells.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PR is not only a progesterone receptor but also a corticosteroid receptor.
PR and corticosteroid receptors share overlapping activity in meditating focal adhesion but have distinct activity in cell proliferation.
PR is a major mediator of the effects of glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids in breast cancer cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids are potential progesterone agonists and may have therapeutic implications in the treatment of progesterone-responsive breast tumors.
PR is not the only receptor for progesterone.
glucocorticoids and mineralocorticoids may play an important role in breast cancer by modulating the effects of progsterone.
